tickets.title: P2-78: PerInstrumentRiskConfig carries two fields nothing reads -- delete them
tickets.defect:
`PerInstrumentRiskConfig` (addons/RiskGuardAddOn.cs:6185) has three fields. Only `MaxContracts` is read, at RiskGuardAddOn.cs:1881, where an order exceeding the per-instrument cap is queued for cancellation.

`IsBlocked` has ZERO references anywhere in the tree. `StopOffsetTicks` appears only at its own declaration.

`IsBlocked` is the more misleading of the two, and it is why this is not merely tidiness. Blocking an instrument is really done through the separate `_config.BlockedInstruments` list (RiskGuardAddOn.cs:1870), which cancels orders on a blacklisted root. So the config offers TWO ways to block an instrument -- a per-instrument `IsBlocked: true` sitting right next to a `MaxContracts` that works, and a top-level list -- and only the list does anything. An operator who writes `InstrumentLimits: { "NQ": { "IsBlocked": true } }` has written something that parses, persists, round-trips through /api/riskguard/config, and protects nothing.

That is the same class as P1-77 (a rule configured and evaluated nowhere) and P1-81 (a control that controls nothing): config that reads as protection which does not exist.
tickets.spec:
DELETE the two dead fields from `PerInstrumentRiskConfig` in addons/RiskGuardAddOn.cs.

1. Remove `public bool IsBlocked { get; set; } = false;`
2. Remove `public double StopOffsetTicks { get; set; } = 40;`
3. `MaxContracts` STAYS. It is the only member of this type the guard reads and the suite drives it (TestPerInstrumentSizing_MNQVsMES, TestMultipleInstrumentsNoPerInstrumentBreach).

Leave a comment at the deletion site recording WHY they went and, specifically, that blocking has exactly ONE mechanism -- `BlockedInstruments` -- so a future reader does not re-add a per-instrument blocking flag believing it to be missing. Reference P2-78.

JSON COMPATIBILITY: an operator's risk_config.json may still contain these keys. They must be SILENTLY IGNORED, not rejected. This type is deserialized by Json.NET, whose default MissingMemberHandling is Ignore, so plain deletion already gives the right behaviour -- do NOT add MissingMemberHandling.Error, and do NOT add validation that throws on unknown keys.

DO NOT: touch addons/GuardRules.cs (already done by hand, and a guard test proves it); touch any *Tests.cs file; keep either field behind [Obsolete] or [JsonIgnore] -- that keeps the lie and makes it quieter, which is the exact remedy this repo rejected on P1-81; 'fix' IsBlocked by wiring it up to the cancel path at :1870 (see context); rename anything; or reformat lines you are not deleting.
tickets.context:
THE ALTERNATIVE REMEDY WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED. `IsBlocked` could be made real by consulting it in the same check that reads `BlockedInstruments` at RiskGuardAddOn.cs:1870. That is deliberately NOT this ticket. Two mechanisms for one outcome is how an operator ends up believing an instrument is blocked because one of the two says so, and this repo has already paid for a second answer to a safety question (see P3-34, the copier's own mode, and P1-81, a second arming flag). One question, one answer. If per-instrument blocking is ever genuinely wanted it belongs as a deliberate feature with its own tests, not as a resurrection of a field that has never worked.

`StopOffsetTicks` has no such argument on either side -- nothing has ever read it and no rule refers to it.

WHY THE COMMENT MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL HERE: the deletion removes the only evidence that anyone ever considered per-instrument blocking. Without a note the next person to read `BlockedInstruments` may well add exactly the field being deleted.

regions.note: The whole type -- six lines. Emit it with the two dead properties removed, MaxContracts unchanged, and a comment recording that BlockedInstruments is the one blocking mechanism. This is the ONLY region; the change is three lines and needs no other file.
